title: Chapter 9. THEY FIGHT THE INVISIBLE BEARS
chineseTitle: 第9章 他们对抗无形的熊

paragraphs.en: The strangers sat down at the table, eager to eat as the platters were filled with delicious food. Each plate held a dama-fruit, whose sweet aroma was too tempting for some.
paragraphs.zh: 陌生人坐到桌旁，迫不及待地想要开吃，因为盘子里盛满了美味佳肴。每碟菜中都放着一种大玛果，那种甜美的香气令人难以抗拒。

paragraphs.en: Dorothy and her companions resisted eating the fruits, fearing invisibility. "Why don't you eat them?" asked one woman.
paragraphs.zh: 多萝西和她的同伴们拒绝吃那些水果，担心会因此变得看不见。“你们为什么不吃呢？”一个女人问道。

paragraphs.en: "We don't want to become invisible," replied Dorothy.
paragraphs.zh: “我们不想变得无形。”多萝西回答道。

paragraphs.en: A child explained, "If we stay visible, the bears will see us and eat us." Another child added, "Here, being invisible is better because we can still hug and kiss each other safely."
paragraphs.zh: 一个孩子解释说：“如果我们保持可见，熊就会看到我们并吃掉我们。”另一个孩子补充道：“在这里，隐形更好，因为我们还能安全地拥抱和亲吻对方。”

paragraphs.en: The man noted, "And we don’t have to worry about our appearance as much." The second child chimed in, "Mama can't tell if my face is dirty!"
paragraphs.zh: 那人说道：“所以我们不必太在意自己的外表。”二儿子接口道：“妈妈根本看不出来我的脸脏不脏！”

paragraphs.en: The mother retorted, "I make you wash it every time I think of it. Your face must be dirty whether I see it or not."
paragraphs.zh: 母亲反驳道：“我每次想到这件事就会让你洗，你脸脏是肯定的，我看不见也一样。”

paragraphs.en: Dorothy invited Ianu and his sister to come closer. She gently touched their faces and forms, deciding one was a girl around her age and the other a smaller boy. The girl's soft, fluffy hair and smooth skin impressed Dorothy.
paragraphs.zh: 多萝西邀请伊努和他的妹妹靠近一些。她轻柔地摸了摸他们的脸庞和身形，判断其中一个是与自己年龄相仿的女孩，另一个则是稍小的男孩。女孩柔软蓬松的头发和光滑细腻的皮肤给多萝西留下了深刻的印象。

paragraphs.en: "If I could see you, you would be beautiful," she said. The mother explained that in Voe Valley, beauty is not vainly displayed but appreciated through good actions and nature’s beauties like flowers and skies.
paragraphs.zh: “如果你在我眼前，你会更加美丽。”她说。母亲解释道，在沃伊山谷，美丽并非空洞地展现，而是通过良好的行为和大自然的美景如花朵与天空来欣赏。

paragraphs.en: Zeb asked about birds, beasts, and fishes. "We can’t see the bears or birds because they eat dama-fruit too," replied one of the children. "But we enjoy their songs and catch fish from our brooks."
paragraphs.zh: 泽布询问起鸟兽鱼虫：“我们看不见熊和鸟，因为它们也吃大马果。”一个孩子回答说，“但我们能享受它们的歌声，并从溪流中捕获鱼类。”

paragraphs.en: The Wizard remarked, "You have much to be happy about even when unseen." He added, "But let's remain visible while here."
paragraphs.zh: 巫师说道：“即使看不见，你们也有很多值得高兴的事。”他又补充道：“不过在这里我们还是保持可见吧。”

paragraphs.en: Eureka entered the room, having wandered outside with Jim. Seeing the food on the table, she cried out, "Now feed me, Dorothy; I'm half starved."
paragraphs.zh: 欧瑞卡走进房间，她和吉姆在外边闲逛了一圈。看到餐桌上摆着食物，不禁喊道：“多萝西，快给我吃东西；我都半饥半渴了。”

paragraphs.en: Dorothy reassured them that Eureka was a harmless pet. The kitten then jumped onto a chair and pawed at the cloth to see what was there. Suddenly, an unseen hand grabbed her, suspending her in mid-air.
paragraphs.zh: 多萝西向他们保证，尤里卡是一只无害的小猫。小猫随后跳上了一把椅子，用爪子拨弄着布料，想看看下面有什么。突然间，一只看不见的手抓住了她，将她悬在半空中。

paragraphs.en: Terrified, Eureka struggled but was dropped when the hand released her.
paragraphs.zh: 惊恐之下，尤里卡挣扎着想要逃脱，但当那双手松开了她，她还是被放了下来。

paragraphs.en: "Did you see that, Dorothy?" Eureka gasped.
paragraphs.zh: “你看到了没有，多萝西？”尤里卡惊呼道。

paragraphs.en: "Yes," replied Dorothy, "there are people here we can't see. You must behave better or something worse will happen."
paragraphs.zh: “是的，”多萝西回答，“这里有一些我们看不见的人。你必须表现得更好一点，否则会有更糟的事情发生。”

paragraphs.en: Dorothy placed a plate of food on the floor for Eureka to eat. The kitten devoured it eagerly and then begged for some fruit she had seen earlier.
paragraphs.zh: 多萝西在地板上放了一盘食物给厄瑞卡吃。这只小猫狼吞虎咽地吃完后，又乞求主人再给它一些之前看到的水果。

paragraphs.en: "These are damas," explained Dorothy, warning that tasting them would make Eureka invisible. The kitten looked longingly at the fruit but decided not to touch it.
paragraphs.zh: “这些是达玛果，”多萝西解释道，警告说尝了它们会让尤里卡变得看不见。小猫羡慕地盯着那些果实，但最终决定不去碰它。

paragraphs.en: The Wizard addressed the air, asking if there was a way out of the valley. A voice replied that leaving was easy but entering an unpleasant country was necessary. Reaching the top of the earth was impossible, and one might fall off if they tried.
paragraphs.zh: 巫师对着空气问道，是否有办法离开这个山谷。一个声音回答说，离开是容易的，但进入一个不愉快的国度则是必要的。想要到达地球的顶端是不可能的，如果尝试的话可能会摔下去。

paragraphs.en: Dorothy interjected, "We've been there before, so we know."
paragraphs.zh: 多萝西插嘴道：“我们去过那个地方，所以心里有数。”

paragraphs.en: The Wizard continued, "The Valley of Voe is charming, but we must move on. Even unpleasant places are necessary to reach the earth's surface."
paragraphs.zh: 巫师继续说道：“沃谷虽然景色宜人，但我们还是得继续前行。即使是不愉快的地方，也是我们必须经过的。”

paragraphs.en: "Then it seems best for us to cross your valley," said the man, "and climb the spiral staircase inside Pyramid Mountain. The top is lost in clouds, and that’s where the Gargoyles live."
paragraphs.zh: “那么看来最好的办法就是穿过您的山谷，”那人说道，“然后爬上金字塔山内的螺旋楼梯。山顶被云雾笼罩，那里正是石像鬼的栖息地。”

paragraphs.en: "What are Gargoyles?" asked Zeb.
paragraphs.zh: “什么是石像鬼？”泽布问道。

paragraphs.en: "I don't know," replied the man. "Overman-Anu once fought them for nine days but never described them. He was eaten by a bear afterward."
paragraphs.zh: “我不知道，”那人回答道。“奥弗曼-阿努曾与它们搏斗了九天，但从未描述过那些东西。后来他被一只熊吃掉了。”

paragraphs.en: The group felt discouraged, but Dorothy said, "If we must face the Gargoyles to get home, then so be it. They can’t be worse than the Wicked Witch or Nome King."
paragraphs.zh: 小组成员有些气馁，但多萝西说道：“如果我们必须面对石像怪兽才能回家，那也没办法。它们肯定不会比恶毒女巫或名王更糟糕。”

paragraphs.en: "Remember," suggested the Wizard, "you had help from the Scarecrow and Tin Woodman before. Now there’s no warrior in your company."
paragraphs.zh: “记得吗？”巫师建议说，“你之前得到了稻草人和铁皮人相助。现在你们队伍里没有战士了。”

paragraphs.en: "Oh, I think Zeb could fight if he needed to," said Dorothy.
paragraphs.zh: “哦，我觉得zepter如果需要的话还是能打一仗的。”多萝西说道。

paragraphs.en: "Perhaps," answered Zeb doubtfully.
paragraphs.zh: “也许吧，”赛布犹疑地回答道。

paragraphs.en: "And you have that jointed sword you used on the vegetable Sorcerer," she added.
paragraphs.zh: “你还有那把关节剑，上次用来对付蔬菜巫师的。”她补充道。

paragraphs.en: "True," agreed Zeb. "I also have other useful things in my satchel."
paragraphs.zh: “确实,” 贾布同意道，“我的小包里还有一些别的有用的东西。”

paragraphs.en: The man's voice then interjected, "Gargoyles fear noise most. Our Champion said shouting his battle-cry made them shudder and retreat."
paragraphs.zh: 那人的话紧接着插嘴道：“石像鬼最怕噪音。我们的冠军说，他喊出战吼就能让他们浑身一震，退避三舍。”

paragraphs.en: "We can all yell better than fight," said the Wizard. "We should defeat the Gargoyles that way."
paragraphs.zh: “我们大喊的效果比战斗更好，”巫师说道，“我们应该用这种方式击败石像鬼。”

paragraphs.en: "But how did Overman-Anu let bears eat him?" asked Dorothy. "And if both were invisible, who knows they ate him?"
paragraphs.zh: “可是Overman-Anu怎么会任由熊吃掉呢？”多萝西问道，“而且如果两者都是隐形的，谁知道是被吃了呢？”

paragraphs.en: The unseen man revealed that the Champion had killed eleven bears, as evidenced by the disappearance of their charm after death. When the Champion was slain, his body parts were visible until consumed by the bears.
paragraphs.zh: 看不见的人透露，冠军曾杀死过十一头熊，这从它们死亡后失去魔力的迹象可以证明。当冠军被击败时，他的身体部位在被熊吞噬之前清晰可见。

paragraphs.en: They bid farewell to the kind but unseen cottage dwellers and set off again, following a broad stream past several more cottages. They found plenty of fruits and flowers, including many damas favored by Voe's people.
paragraphs.zh: 他们告别了那些和善却未曾谋面的农舍主人，再次启程。沿途是一条宽阔的小溪，旁边还有几座农舍。他们发现这里果实累累、花香四溢，其中不乏沃斯族人所钟爱的多玛果。

paragraphs.en: At noon, they stopped in an orchard for Jim to rest. Suddenly, a soft voice warned them about nearby bears. The Wizard drew his sword, Zeb grabbed the horse-whip, and Dorothy climbed into the buggy with Jim grazing nearby.
paragraphs.zh: 中午时分，他们在一片果园里停了下来，让吉姆休息。突然，一个温柔的声音警告他们附近有熊出没。巫师拔出了剑，泽比格抓起了马鞭，多萝西则坐进了马车，而吉姆就在附近照料着牲口。

paragraphs.en: The unseen voice laughed and said escape was impossible that way. Instead, it advised taking to the river, as the bears would not venture onto water. Concerned they might drown, Dorothy asked if there was no danger.
paragraphs.zh: 无形的声音笑了，说那样逃跑是不可能的。相反，它建议她们向河边走，因为熊不会冒险涉水。担心可能会溺水，多萝西问道是否有其他危险。

paragraphs.en: The gentle voice explained they were strangers in Voe Valley and offered help.
paragraphs.zh: 温柔的声音解释说他们是 Voel 山谷的陌生人，并主动提供了帮助。

paragraphs.en: In an instant, a broad-leaved plant appeared before the Wizard. The voice instructed him to rub the leaves on his soles, allowing them to walk on water without sinking. This secret was unknown to the bears, and people of Voe used it to avoid enemies while traveling.
paragraphs.zh: 瞬间，一片宽大的植物出现在巫师面前。声音指示他将叶片在脚底摩擦，从而能够在水上行走而不下沉。这一秘密对熊来说是未知的，而沃伊的人们则利用这一点，在旅行中避开敌人。

paragraphs.en: The Wizard cried out in joy and rubbed a leaf on Dorothy's shoes, then on his own. She handed a leaf to Zeb, who applied it to her feet before rubbing it on Jim’s hooves and the buggy wheels. As he finished, they heard a low growl and saw the horse jump and kick viciously.
paragraphs.zh: 巫师欣喜若狂地喊道，将一片叶子擦在多萝西的鞋上，随后也擦了擦自己的鞋子。她递给泽布一片叶子，泽布先将它敷在她的脚上，再抹在吉姆的蹄子和马车轮子上。他刚完成这个动作，就听到一声低沉的 growl，并看到那匹马猛地一跳，凶猛地尥起了蹶子。

paragraphs.en: "Quick! To the water!" their unseen friend shouted.
paragraphs.zh: “快！去喝水！”他们那位无形的朋友喊道。

paragraphs.en: The Wizard drove the buggy down the riverbank. Dorothy remained in the buggy with Eureka, which did not sink due to the plant's properties. When they reached the middle of the stream, Zeb ran across the water towards them.
paragraphs.zh: 巫师驾着马车沿着河岸前行。多萝西和尤里卡留在马车上，由于植物的特性，马车并未下沉。当他们来到河流中央时，赛布从水面上跑向他们。

paragraphs.en: The horse was thrashing wildly, with deep gashes on its sides from unseen attackers. The Wizard shouted for Jim to run to the river. Jim kicked off his tormentors and followed, finding safety in the water.
paragraphs.zh: 马匹疯狂地踢踏着，两侧被不明攻击者留下了几道深深的伤痕。巫师喊着让吉姆跑到河边。吉姆摆脱了纠缠他的敌人，跟着跑了过去，在河水中找到了安全。

paragraphs.en: Zeb joined them as they floated downstream.
paragraphs.zh: 泽布加入了他们，顺流而下。

paragraphs.en: Suddenly, a hot breath against his cheek alerted the Wizard, who stabbed at the air with his sword, drawing blood each time. A loud roar and fall revealed a large red bear, nearly as big as the horse, dead from the sword thrusts. The Wizard, seeing its claws and teeth, panicked and rushed into the water.
paragraphs.zh: 突然，一股热气拂过他的脸颊，巫师警觉起来，挥剑向空中刺去，每次挥剑都划破了空气。一声震耳欲聋的吼声和坠落声暴露了一只巨大的红熊，几乎与马一般大小，已被利剑刺死。巫师见到它的利爪和尖牙，顿时慌了神，冲进了水中。

paragraphs.en: On the river, they seemed safe. Dorothy and the buggy floated downstream, while Zeb quickly joined them. The Wizard used sticking plaster to mend Jim’s claw wounds.
paragraphs.zh: 在河上，他们似乎安全无虞。多萝西和马车顺流而下，而泽布迅速加入了她们的行列。巫师用创可贴为吉姆修补了爪伤。

paragraphs.en: Dorothy suggested they follow the river, noting their unknown friend had saved them. The Wizard agreed, as the river led towards Pyramid Mountain, making travel easier.
paragraphs.zh: 多萝西建议他们顺着河流走，指出那位未知的朋友曾救过他们。巫师赞同这个想法，因为河流的方向指向了金字塔山，这样行走会方便许多。

paragraphs.en: Zeb hitched Jim to the buggy again, and the horse trotted smoothly over the water. Initially terrified of getting wet, Eureka soon calmed down and happily ran alongside the vehicle. A fish swam too close, and Eureka quickly ate it, but Dorothy warned her about the enchanted valley's dangers.
paragraphs.zh: 泽布再次将吉姆拴回马车，马儿平稳地涉过水面。起初对弄湿自己感到害怕的尤里卡很快镇定下来，欢快地在车辆旁奔跑。一条鱼游得太近了，尤里卡迅速把它吃掉了，但多萝西警告她不要靠近那个充满魔力的山谷。

paragraphs.en: After several hours, they reached a river bend where they needed to cross a mile before reaching Pyramid Mountain. Few houses or orchards were in sight, making them wary of encountering more savage bears.
paragraphs.zh: 几个小时后，他们来到了一个河湾处，需要再走一英里才能到达金字塔山。眼前很少见到房屋或果园，让他们对可能遇到更凶猛的野熊感到警惕。

paragraphs.en: "Run as fast as you can," instructed the Wizard to Jim.
paragraphs.zh: “你赶紧跑起来，”巫师对吉姆吩咐道。

paragraphs.en: "All right," replied Jim, though he admitted his age made him slower than before.
paragraphs.zh: “好吧，”吉姆回答道，虽然他承认自己的年龄让他没有以前那么敏捷了。

paragraphs.en: They climbed into the buggy, and Zeb took the reins. As soon as they hit land, Jim galloped towards the mountain, making Dorothy gasp with excitement.
paragraphs.zh: 他们跳上马车，泽布握紧缰绳。一踏上陆地，吉姆便纵马奔向山峦， Dorothy 不禁兴奋地倒抽了一口冷气。

paragraphs.en: Zeb then growled like an invisible bear, startling Jim who sped up even more. His legs moved so fast they were barely visible, and the Wizard held on tightly while shouting "Whoa!" at full volume.
paragraphs.zh: 接着，赛布像一只无形的熊一样低吼了一声，吓得吉姆加速跑得更快了。他的双腿快得几乎看不见，巫师紧紧抓住他，大声喊道：“吁！”

paragraphs.en: Dorothy feared Jim was running away, but Zeb assured her that no bear could catch him in such a pace, and neither would the harness or buggy break.
paragraphs.zh: 多萝西担心吉姆要逃跑，但赛布安慰她说，以吉姆的速度，任何熊都追不上他，马具或马车也不会散架。

paragraphs.en: Jim slowed down gradually but abruptly stopped at the foot of the mountain. The Wizard and Zeb were thrown forward, landing in the soft grass below—rolling a few times before they settled. Dorothy held on tightly to the iron rail and avoided being flung out.
paragraphs.zh: 吉姆逐渐减速，但突然在山脚下停了下来。巫师和泽布被猛地向前一推，栽进了下面柔软的草地上——滚了几圈才停下来。多萝西紧紧抓住铁栏杆，避免被甩出去。

paragraphs.en: However, she squeezed Toto so hard that it let out a loud screech. The old cab-horse then made some odd noises, which suggested he was laughing at their predicament.
paragraphs.zh: 然而，她用力捏了捏托托，竟让它发出一声尖锐的叫声。那匹老马车马上也发出了一些奇怪的声音，仿佛在嘲笑他们的困境。
